correctness.rationale: For every lambda in algebraically closed characteristic two, Witt subtraction and a square-root change identify the curve with y²+y=t³, v²+v=y³+b y. Two one-pole degree-two covers have lower conductors 3 and 9, giving genus six, pole weights 4,6,9, and div(dt)=10P∞. Six differentials with distinct nonnegative orders span the canonical six-dimensional space. The characteristic-two formula C((A²+tB²)dt)=Bdt yields explicit images of all six basis elements, with semilinear power ranks 6,4,3,2,1,0 independent of b. Symbolic reduction over F2[c,t,y,v] and four GF4 parameter rank replays passed; finite tests are only corroboration.

originality.rationale: The exact C12 genus-six one-parameter family and its wild ramification are published in Kazemifard–Tafazolian (2026), Theorem 5.8, but that classification does not compute the Cartier action on regular differentials. The present explicit basis and complete power-rank filtration are not consequences of genus, ramification signature, or the published group classification alone. Groen (2022/2024) establishes bounds and an exact ordinary-base case, whereas this intermediate elliptic base is supersingular. Searches of public literature and published mathematical results found no statement that implies the six exact ranks on this family. Historical priority is not certified.
residual_risks: The search does not prove priority; an older classification of Cartier operators for genus-six one-point Witt covers could encompass this example implicitly.
Groen gives general inequalities, and a more precise specialization elsewhere might provide equivalent values; no such published exact specialization was identified.

value.rationale: The new characteristic-two C12 genus-six family had published cyclic automorphism and ramification data, but its Cartier nilpotency filtration is an important intrinsic Jacobian invariant not fixed by genus or group action alone. Exact a-number 2 and rank sequence of all powers determine a nontrivial piece of its torsion and arithmetic geometry uniformly in the moduli parameter; the marked Weierstrass semigroup gives a coherent explicit geometric realization. The result is structural, natural and not an arbitrary numerical slice.
